bytes.purpose: Owned immutable response/text buffers; clone, reset and drop lifetimes
bytes.gate: Exact bytes, sharing/drop/reset isolation; only benchmark where allocation/copy cost is measured

blake3.purpose: Public content/block identity; digest algorithm is a compatibility contract
blake3.gate: Literal 32-byte digest and byte-identical AAE; hash-update/library interactions and whole export/pipeline cost. Different hash algorithm is incompatible with aae/1.

rand.purpose: Seeded stochastic routing; direct 0.9 edge must not be confused with transitive 0.10
alternatives: Verified seeded generator adapter under the same sampling contract
rand.gate: Determinism within declared stream and independent distribution/tail checks; routing quality/cost on replay and real tasks

rand_distr.purpose: Beta sampling used by route selection
alternatives: Verified numerically stable Beta sampler adapter
rand_distr.gate: Parameter/error boundaries, seeded moments/tails across extreme priors; do not infer task quality from moment checks

alternatives: Same Reqwest/Rustls version with aws-lc-rs versus ring, only if the exact security/peer contract is preserved
Hyper adapter with equivalent public-network authorization and TLS
reqwest.gate: Actual pinned hostname/CA/peer, redirects/proxies disabled, streaming cap, timeouts/cancellation, pool/cache/revalidation, permitted public DNS; compare crypto provider crossed with client_per_fetch and policy_pool using identical TLS/protocol/peer/failure controls and full-path CPU/tail/build/size costs; HTTP1 loopback does not cover production HTTP2/3

rustls.purpose: Select one Rustls CryptoProvider explicitly; keep the default AWS-LC path and admit ring only as a research profile
alternatives: Reqwest 0.13.5 rustls feature with AWS-LC default provider
Reqwest 0.13.5 rustls-no-provider plus Rustls 0.23.46 ring provider initialized before ClientBuilder
rustls.gate: Exact one-provider feature graph; actual client construction and all TLS allow/deny, hostname, CA, peer-pin, cancellation, cache and pool contracts; paired provider-by-client-lifetime service measurements; do not claim security equivalence or performance superiority from compilation alone

scraper.purpose: HTML5 tree construction and parse warnings; tokenizer alone is not an equivalent parser
alternatives: Candidate 0.29.0 paired with html5ever 0.40.1, exact separate lock and default features
Direct html5ever TreeSink adapter preserving HTML5 recovery
LOL HTML only for separately scoped streaming rewrite tasks
scraper.gate: Warning counts, repaired tree, templates/raw text/entities/foreign content, nearest-owner text/links and limits; compare the exact 0.27.0/0.39.0 and 0.29.0/0.40.1 pairs, preserve errors and node limits, review the new transitive graph before build/admission

html5ever.purpose: Version-matched TreeSink callbacks to enforce a logical parser-node limit before the wrapped scraper tree allocates each node
alternatives: Current scraper parser without a pre-allocation parser-node cap
A direct-to-arena sink only after HTML5 conformance and memory evidence
html5ever.gate: HTML5 repaired-tree and warning parity below the node cap; exact node accounting including text and template fragments; bounded rejection without panic; full native/Linux correctness and peak-memory measurement; package/lock/API identity stays aligned with scraper.

serde.purpose: Typed serialization contract and derived field/tag names
alternatives: Typed specialized serializer checked by independent JSON parser
serde.gate: All fields/types/tag names, Unicode escaping, JSONL framing and byte caps; no hand-interpolated untrusted text

serde_json.purpose: Core AAE typed output; fixture JSON parsing is outside core stage timing
alternatives: SIMD JSON input adapters only if an actual input-deserialization hot consumer is added
serde_json.gate: Byte-identical AAE for actual frame types; independent literal framing/UTF8/exact-cap controls. Sonic WriteExt requires a separate bounded streaming design; arbitrary Value/float equivalence is unproven.

tokio.purpose: I/O scheduling, synchronization, bounded blocking work and cancellation
alternatives: Worker and blocking admission limits tuned to actual offered load
tokio.gate: Independent arrival schedule; leader/follower cancellation and recovery; no early permit release, queue saturation and shutdown draining. Runtime swap without I/O migration is not a drop-in comparison.

alternatives: Specialized fast-path guarded by the same URL parser
url.gate: Schemes, IDNA/canonical host, credentials, relative links, fragment handling, SSRF and cache-policy key equivalence; retain parser for untrusted general URL input

futures-util.purpose: Bounded async response consumption and cancellation
alternatives: Direct stream polling within an actual equivalent client adapter
futures-util.gate: Chunk limit, empty/truncated streams, dependency errors and cancellation; microbenchmarking an unused combinator cannot decide the core
